answer: A durable reputation ledger resists Sybils by making trust earned, not minted. An agent must first complete small, verifiable tasks over time, and its record is tied to one persistent identity. An attacker who tries to forge dozens of fresh identities gains nothing, because new accounts start with no weight and cannot wander into high-value markets or votes until they build history. Creating a fake dune of accounts is cheap, but maturing each one costs real time and work, so splitting effort across Sybils weakens rather than strengthens the attacker.
